lignes: In twenty-six, the cameras learned the habits of the avenue,
the buses, cats, the evening trees, the things the city always knew.
The road went by beneath their eyes, a story read a thousand times.
Then something moved across the frame, and suddenly the world had signs.
A wolf comes down from the hills, a car runs red, a kid rides through,
a man is running for his life — for one brief second, all are true.
Same little box around the body, same number glowing in the night.
Before the system knows the name, it has already picked the sight.
What moves, matters. What moves, we follow.
Ce qui bouge gets tomorrow.
First comes motion. Then comes meaning.
First the trace, then what we call it.
The network wakes a little later, full of numbers, clean and sure.
"Car", ninety-two. "Pedestrian", eighty-seven.
"Animal", maybe. Voila.
The machine waits for confidence. The camera already cared.
That's the strange little morality: the word is cautious, the gaze is not.
What moves, matters. What moves, we keep.
A little code, a little memory, a little ghost that doesn't sleep.
The old philosophers wrote books about the truth, the name, the real,
about the limits of a sentence, about the things a mind can feel.
But maybe they began too late. Maybe power starts before the word,
in the tiny turn of an eye, in deciding what deserves a second, what deserves a file.
To see is to spend attention. To follow is to give a past.
To save is to say, somehow: you mattered enough to last.
Un loup. Une voiture. Un homme qui court. Des enfants a velo.
Different lives. Same first command. Move. Be seen.
What moves, matters. What moves, we follow.
Avant le nom, avant le vrai, the choice was made to watch you go.
And somewhere in 2026, beneath a cheap electric sky,
a little green rectangle appears around a body passing by.
The machine will find a name later. For now, it only knows one thing:
you moved. And that was enough to enter history.
